name: workspace.connectAgent
title: Connect AI agent
summary: The setup that connects an AI agent's client to the MCP server of this workspace: a command for the terminal or a JSON block, with the absolute paths of this installation; for Claude Code also an entry for `.mcp.json`. Creates and changes no file and opens no connection.
details: Clients: `claude-code` (Claude Code), `claude-desktop` (Claude Desktop), `cursor` (Cursor), `vscode` (VS Code), `codex-cli` (Codex CLI) and `other`. Without a client the output lists them. Claude Code, VS Code and Codex CLI get a command for the terminal (PowerShell on Windows); Claude Desktop and Cursor a JSON block with the file it belongs in on this system; `other` a JSON block in the common `mcpServers` form. For every client but Claude Desktop, `next` also names the call of `tool guide --skill --write` for the workspace, with the same program, as a command for the terminal (PowerShell on Windows), which writes the skill file. For Claude Code, `mcpJson` also gives an entry for the file `.mcp.json` in the root of the Git repository the workspace folder lies in (without Git, in the workspace folder): it starts `reqseq` from the PATH with the workspace path relative to that folder, once for macOS and Linux and once for Windows through `cmd /c`; the Windows form is left out when that path holds a space or one of `&^%<>|!"(),;=\`. The server is named `reqseq`: a second workspace in the same client, or in the same Git repository, needs another name. On macOS, an app that runs from the temporary place the system gives a downloaded app that was not moved gets no setup (`agent.app-translocated`).
